Rule.name: Lunar New Year
Rule.comment: The first day of the first month of the Chinese lunisolar year. Also celebrated as Tết (Vietnam) and Seollal (Korea). Falls between 21 January and 20 February in the Gregorian calendar. Resolved via the Fixed strategy using ChineseLunisolarCalendar (month 1, day 1).

Rule.name: Lantern Festival
Rule.comment: Yuanxiao Jie. Falls on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month, fourteen days after Lunar New Year, marking the end of the New Year festival period. Observed with lantern displays, riddle games, and the eating of tangyuan (sweet rice dumplings). Resolved via OffsetFromAnchor from Lunar New Year (+14 days).

Rule.name: Qingming Festival
Rule.comment: Qingming Jie (清明節), also known as Tomb-Sweeping Day or Pure Brightness Festival. A solar term that falls on the fifteenth day after the Spring Equinox, typically 4–5 April. Families visit and clean the graves of their ancestors, making offerings of food, flowers, and paper goods. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'qingming'.

Rule.name: Dragon Boat Festival
Rule.comment: Duanwu Jie (端午節). Falls on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, typically in June. Commemorates the poet and statesman Qu Yuan and is observed with dragon boat races and the eating of zongzi (sticky rice dumplings). Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'dragon-boat-festival'.

Rule.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
Rule.comment: Zhongqiu Jie (中秋節), also known as the Moon Festival or Mooncake Festival. Falls on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, when the moon is at its fullest and brightest. Observed with mooncakes, lanterns, and family reunions. Widely celebrated in China, Vietnam, Korea, and Chinese diaspora communities worldwide. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'mid-autumn-festival'.

Rule.name: Double Ninth Festival
Rule.comment: Chongyang Jie (重陽節), also known as the Chrysanthemum Festival. Falls on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. Traditionally observed by climbing mountains, drinking chrysanthemum wine, and paying respects to ancestors. In many jurisdictions the day is also designated as Seniors' Day. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'double-ninth-festival'.
